items.title: Democrats sweep midterms, gain control of Congress
items.feedTitle: Midterm voters rebuke Trump, handing Democrats both chambers of Congress
items.summary: Voters delivered a decisive rebuke to President Trump and Republicans in Tuesday's midterm elections, handing Democrats major victories and control of both chambers of Congress. The results dramatically reshape the balance of power in Washington, with Trump entering a lame-duck phase of his second term. The election saw historic firsts, including the first Native American woman governor elected in New Mexico and other breakthrough winners across multiple states.

items.title: Three injured in shooting at Des Moines post office
items.feedTitle: 3 people injured in shooting at Des Moines post office; suspect detained
items.summary: Three people were injured in a shooting at a post office in Des Moines, Iowa, with police saying the suspect was an employee at the facility. The incident resulted in multiple injuries and the suspect was detained at the scene. The shooting marked one of several mass casualty incidents across the country during the reporting period.

items.title: Record flash flooding swamps Tennessee and Georgia
items.feedTitle: Record flash flooding swamps Tennessee, Georgia towns
items.summary: Record flash flooding swept through communities along the Georgia-Tennessee border, forcing dozens of rescues despite hazardous conditions. The National Weather Service issued flood warnings urging residents to seek higher ground immediately. The severe storms brought heavy rain that inundated the region overnight and into Thursday morning.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces international retirement
items.feedTitle: Cristiano Ronaldo announces his international retirement from Portugal
items.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo, 41, announced his retirement from international football, ending a 23-year career spanning six World Cups. The Portugal superstar's decision came after a falling-out with head coach Jorge Jesus. Ronaldo holds the men's all-time international scoring record and won the European Championship with Portugal.

items.title: Justice Department civil rights head Dhillon resigns
items.feedTitle: Head of Justice Department office on Civil Rights resigns
items.summary: Harmeet Dhillon, the head of the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division, resigned after 18 months in the position. She is the first major Trump appointee to resign following the Republican midterm losses. Dhillon's departure marks a significant exit from the administration after what political observers characterized as a tumultuous tenure.

stlouis.title: Black voters fuel Democratic wave in St. Louis region
stlouis.feedTitle: Black voters help fuel Democratic wave
stlouis.summary: Black voters played a pivotal role in driving the Democratic wave that swept the region and nation during the midterm elections. The strong turnout and voting patterns helped Democrats win historic victories across St. Louis and surrounding areas. Voter mobilization efforts succeeded in energizing key constituencies in the metro area.

stlouis.title: Planned Parenthood charts path after Missouri rejects Amendment 3
stlouis.feedTitle: Planned Parenthood looks ahead after Missouri rejects Amendment 3
stlouis.summary: Planned Parenthood announced plans to move forward after Missouri voters rejected Amendment 3 in the midterm elections. The vote was a setback for abortion rights restrictions in the state. The organization is now evaluating its strategic options and operations in Missouri.

stlouis.title: St. Louis police deploy drones for first 911 responses
stlouis.feedTitle: St. Louis police drone unit responds to first 911 call hours after program approval
stlouis.summary: The St. Louis Police Department's newly approved drone unit responded to its first 911 call just hours after program approval was finalized. The deployment marks the beginning of operational use of unmanned aircraft for emergency response. The initiative represents a new tool in the department's incident response capabilities.

items.title: UK court convicts Russell Brand of rape and sexual assault
items.feedTitle: Comedian Russell Brand found guilty by UK court of rape and sexual assaults
items.summary: Comedian Russell Brand was found guilty by a UK court of raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others, concluding a years-long legal saga. The judge indicated Brand faces a 'significant custodial term.' The conviction raises questions about how Brand was able to continue his career despite allegations and accusations spanning multiple years.

items.title: Bomb threats disrupt at least 22 flights across Europe
items.feedTitle: Bomb threats disrupt at least 22 flights across Europe, raising hybrid war fears
items.summary: Bomb threats caused diversions and emergency landings for at least 22 commercial flights across Europe, with officials calling the incidents 'malicious hoaxes.' The coordinated nature of the threats raised questions about a possible hybrid war effort to disrupt European air travel. EU transport officials said it was too early to confirm whether the threats were linked.

items.title: Paraguay president resigns after bank collapse crisis
items.feedTitle: Paraguay President Santiago Peña resigns after bank collapse
items.summary: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña resigned following the collapse of a digital bank that left millions unable to access their money. The move came after the lower house of Congress voted to pursue an impeachment trial against him. The bank collapse and ensuing crisis destabilized the country's financial system.

items.title: Bank of England raises rates for first time in three years
items.feedTitle: Bank of England raises interest rates to 4%, the first increase for more than three years
items.summary: The Bank of England raised its base rate to 4% for the first time in more than three years, an increase from 3.75%. The bank's governor signaled another rate rise may be forthcoming to combat rising inflation. The decision came amid concerns about cost-of-living pressures on households.

items.title: French unions launch nationwide strikes over living costs
items.feedTitle: French protests see numbers surge as unions join strikes over high cost of living
items.summary: French trade unions organized nationwide protests and general strikes over rising costs and deteriorating public services, with the interior ministry estimating 600,000 participants. Union leaders claim the numbers were significantly higher. The demonstrations reflect growing anger over economic conditions and wage demands.

items.title: Jaypal Malviya wins silver, secures India's first LA28 shooting quota
items.feedTitle: Jaypal Malviya wins silver, secures India's first shooting quota for 2028 Olympics; Manu, Suruchi falter
items.summary: Shooter Jaypal Malviya captured silver at the ISSF World Championships and secured India's first Olympic quota for shooting at the 2028 Los Angeles Games. The first-time championship competitor's achievement marks a significant milestone for Indian shooting. Her success also qualifies her for the upcoming Olympic cycle.

items.title: India hockey team retains Asian Champions Trophy with Japan victory
items.feedTitle: How India overcame a 1-0 deficit and smashed Japan to defend Asian Champions Trophy
items.summary: India's hockey team defeated Japan 4-1 in the Asian Champions Trophy final to claim their record sixth title and complete an unbeaten campaign. India's comeback from a 1-0 deficit demonstrated the team's resilience and skill. The victory reinforced India's dominance in regional hockey competition.

items.title: Foreign Secretary Misri sets stage for Nepal PM’s upcoming India visit
items.feedTitle: Foreign Secretary Misri sets stage for Nepal PM’s upcoming India visit
items.summary: Summary unavailable for this update.

items.title: India test-fires Pralay quasi-ballistic missile successfully
items.feedTitle: 500-km range, 1,000-kg payload: India test-fires quasi-ballistic missile Pralay
items.summary: The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) successfully tested the indigenously developed Pralay quasi-ballistic missile. The test demonstrated the weapon's 500-km range and 1,000-kg payload capacity. The successful test showcases India's advancing indigenous defense capabilities.

items.title: Devi Shetty honored with France's National Order of Merit
items.feedTitle: Devi Shetty conferred with France’s National Order of Merit
items.summary: Dr. Devi Shetty was conferred France's National Order of Merit in recognition of his contributions to healthcare and pandemic relief efforts. He was recognized for extending vaccination support and logistical assistance to the French Consulate and broader French community during the pandemic. The honor reflects his international humanitarian work.

immigration.title: Democratic Congress could reshape H-1B visa policy framework
immigration.feedTitle: Democratic Control of Congress Could Reshape H-1B Visa Policy and U.S.-India Trade Relations
immigration.summary: With Democrats now controlling Congress following the midterm elections, H-1B visa policy faces potential scrutiny and possible changes. Democratic-led committees are expected to increase oversight of restrictions on the temporary work visa program. The shift in congressional power may alter the trajectory of Trump administration immigration enforcement policies, though immediate relief for visa holders is unlikely.

immigration.title: USCIS guidance: temporary visa holders must leave US to apply for green card
immigration.feedTitle: Temporary visa holders may have to leave the US to apply for a green card under new USCIS guidance
immigration.summary: Under new USCIS guidance, temporary visa holders may be required to depart the United States to apply for green card sponsorship rather than adjusting status from within the country. This directive represents a shift in adjustment-of-status procedures. Visa holders and their employers face uncertainty about the practical implications and timeline for implementation (proposed, not finalized as of report date).

immigration.title: USCIS citizenship test expanded to 128 questions with higher passing requirement
immigration.feedTitle: Confirmed by USCIS | The citizenship test got harder: there are now 128 questions, and you have to get more right
immigration.summary: USCIS confirmed an expansion of the citizenship naturalization test, which now includes 128 questions requiring a higher percentage correct to pass. The increased difficulty and scope represents a tightening of citizenship requirements. The changes take effect under current administration policy (finalized and in effect).

items.title: Nasdaq plunges toward worst day in 18 months amid AI selloff
items.feedTitle: Nasdaq heading for worst day in 18 months as Wall Street sustains widespread losses
items.summary: The tech-heavy Nasdaq share index dropped as much as 5% on Thursday in its worst day in 18 months, driven by a sharp selloff in AI-related stocks and semiconductor companies. The selloff wiped out approximately $2.2 trillion in market value. The decline was attributed to concerns that a Democratic-controlled Congress could impose tougher regulation on the artificial intelligence industry.

items.title: US stocks plunge after midterm rally reversal; oil prices tumble
items.feedTitle: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq plunge in dramatic reversal, giving back post-election rally gains
items.summary: US stock markets experienced a dramatic reversal after the midterm elections, with major indices giving back post-election gains. Oil prices fell sharply following Democratic victories and Vice President Vance's statements questioning the Iran war strategy. The sell-off reflected shifting investor sentiment on policy implications of Democratic congressional control.

items.title: Indian markets surge for sixth day; Sensex gains 2,009 points
items.feedTitle: Investors richer by Rs 29 lakh crore as Sensex, Nifty rise over 8%; FIIs pour in money, but will rally la
items.summary: Indian stock markets extended their winning streak to six consecutive sessions, with the Sensex rising 2,009 points and Nifty reclaiming the 24,500 level for the first time in three months. Investor wealth increased by approximately Rs 29 lakh crore as markets surged more than 8%. Foreign institutional investors poured money into Indian equities amid falling oil prices and cooling AI trade concerns following US midterm results.

items.title: US jobless claims at 57-year lows; worker productivity surges
items.feedTitle: US weekly jobless claims at 57-year lows; worker productivity surges in third quarter
items.summary: Weekly US jobless claims dropped to 57-year lows, with initial filings remaining at 189,000—the fewest since mid-July. Worker productivity surged in the third quarter amid low layoff rates. The data suggests a tight labor market and strong economic fundamentals despite broader equity market volatility.

items.title: Developing nations' debt hits record $9.4 trillion amid rate pressures
items.feedTitle: Debt of poorest countries at record $9.4tn high, World Bank data shows
items.summary: Debt owed by developing countries rose to a record $9.4 trillion last year, with the poorest nations paying the highest interest rates since the late 1980s. The World Bank data shows the cost of servicing external debt is preventing developing countries from investing in future growth. The UK government is preparing plans to address the mounting debt crisis in poorer nations.

finance.note: Oil prices fell to two-month lows after Democratic midterm victories and Vice President Vance's statements questioning the Iran war, with Brent crude dropping 6.5% to $105.55 per barrel. US stocks plunged on Thursday in their worst post-midterm day since 1896, with the Nasdaq entering correction territory (down 4%) amid AI regulation fears and semiconductor selloffs totaling $2.2 trillion in value lost. In contrast, Indian markets surged for a sixth consecutive day, with Sensex up 2,009 points and Nifty reclaiming 24,500 as foreign institutional investors returned on falling oil and cooling AI trade concerns. Watch: whether the tech selloff continues, whether Democratic regulation proposals gain traction, and whether oil remains suppressed.

cards.title: Reframing beats defending
cards.insight: OpenAI didn't argue that data centers are harmless; instead it rebranded them as 'compute campuses' and committed to transparency on costs. When facing entrenched skepticism, audiences often reject defensive claims but accept a new frame that acknowledges legitimate concerns.
cards.takeaway: When your message faces headwinds, ask: what concern is true underneath the opposition, and can I name it differently?

cards.title: Personal stakes move voters more than national narratives
cards.insight: Democratic wins centered on local issues—education policy in Texas, abortion rights in Missouri, cost-of-living pressures in Georgia—rather than abstract ideology. Voters rewarded specificity and connection to everyday life over partisan messaging.
cards.takeaway: Lead with the concrete harm or benefit voters experience, not the principle you want them to embrace.

cards.title: Silence during uncertainty creates space for critics
cards.insight: Trump administration actions on Iran remained unexplained until Vice President Vance's post-election critique surfaced; the lack of transparent communication allowed opposition narratives to dominate and likely contributed to market fear. Proactive transparency reduces speculation damage.
cards.takeaway: When stakes are high and timing is ambiguous, explain decisions early and directly—silence invites opponents to fill the void.

cards.title: Coalition shifts outpace party loyalty messaging
cards.insight: Latino voters swung Democratic, Black voters showed strong turnout, and suburban voters rejected Trump—but Democrats didn't win by lecturing these groups on loyalty. They won by listening to each group's distinct fears (immigration enforcement, education, healthcare) and addressing them.
cards.takeaway: Segment your audience and mirror their language and priorities back; one-size-fits-all messaging alienates those who don't see themselves in it.

ai.title: OpenAI rebrands data centers as 'compute campuses' amid opposition
ai.feedTitle: OpenAI rebrands data centers as ‘compute campuses,’ unveils new framework
ai.summary: OpenAI unveiled a new framework Thursday for building data centers, rebranding them as 'compute campuses' in response to growing public opposition to server warehouses powering the AI boom. The company committed to paying the full cost of electricity consumed by its infrastructure. The rebranding reflects efforts to improve public perception of data center expansion.

ai.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber cybersecurity model
ai.feedTitle: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber with 'Critical' cybersecurity rating
ai.summary: OpenAI debuted GPT-6 Cyber, a new cybersecurity-focused AI model designed to improve vulnerability discovery while incorporating stronger safety guardrails to prevent misuse. The launch comes amid growing concerns about AI-driven cyberattacks and the dual-use nature of security tools. OpenAI says the model performs better than previous versions while maintaining security protections.

ai.title: OpenAI president says company could be IPO-ready by 2027
ai.feedTitle: OpenAI president Greg Brockman says company could be IPO ready in 2027
ai.summary: OpenAI President Greg Brockman said the company could be ready to go public in 2027, pointing to accelerating enterprise revenue and a business turnaround. The statement indicates confidence in the company's financial trajectory and commercialization progress. However, prediction markets suggest an IPO before end of November remains highly unlikely.

ai.title: Anthropic's AI models improving twice as fast with AI assistance
ai.feedTitle: Anthropic's models improving nearly twice as fast with help from AI, study finds
ai.summary: A study found that Anthropic's models are improving nearly twice as fast with the help of AI itself, suggesting a new phase in AI development acceleration. The research indicates that AI systems can substantially boost their own development cycle speed. Meanwhile, reports indicate Anthropic is rapidly accelerating development amid broader calls for AI slowdowns.

ai.title: Dropbox acquires Tigris Data for $350M to enhance AI infrastructure
ai.feedTitle: Dropbox acquires Tigris Data for $350M to bolster its AI infrastructure
ai.summary: Dropbox announced a $350 million acquisition of Tigris Data to bolster its AI infrastructure capabilities. The deal is expected to support development of DBX Agent Cloud, a storage platform aimed at developers building AI models and agents. The acquisition reflects major tech companies' push to build comprehensive AI development platforms.
